channel.title: Orla Brennick Blog
channel.description: Notes from Orla Brennick's studio in Galway, Ireland: wheel-throwing, glazes and reduction firing, drying pots in the Atlantic damp, and how the work actually gets made.

item.title: Why Every Mug Starts as 420 Grams of Clay
item.description: Every mug I make begins on the scale, not the wheel: what weighing clay to the gram settles before the wheel turns, where the 420 grams go, and when I ignore the number.

item.title: What Reduction Firing Actually Does to a Glaze
item.description: On firing days I starve a gas kiln of oxygen on purpose. What that does to iron and copper, why my celadon only exists because of it, and why no two firings match.

item.title: Drying Pots in a City That Is Never Dry
item.description: Why a board of bowls can take a week to firm up in a Galway March, why slow drying is mostly kind to pots, and the plastic collars, damp cupboard and radiator that keep my handles on.
